clue.text: Align IT launch badly — it's an AI problem

indicators.note: something done badly is botched and out of order, so the letters must be rearranged

parts.note: thirteen letters of fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A tech department botches the rollout of a new system, and the trouble is blamed on artificial intelligence.
explanation.walkthrough: The capitalised IT looks like the tech department, but it is just two more letters for the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: When a chatbot confidently invents facts, that failure is called hallucinating in the jargon of machine learning.

clue.text: Hack potentially taking down Leavitt's fake news

indicators.note: one thing taking another has it attached, so the next piece follows on

parts.note: a hack is a riding horse; 'potentially' marks it as one example
down is the soft plumage of birds

explanation.surface: A journalist ends up quoting a White House press secretary's dismissal of a story as fake news.
explanation.walkthrough: Hack reads as a journalist but here it is the horse sense; Karoline Leavitt is a White House press secretary who often brands reports as fake news.
explanation.definitionFit: Horsefeathers is an old American slang exclamation meaning nonsense or rubbish, the kind of retort a spokesperson gives to unwelcome reporting.

clue.text: … as aside, a casual farewell to Gore?

definitions.note: adverb in the clue, the answer is an adjective; 'as aside' means to the side

parts.note: 'later' is a casual way to say goodbye
the person being addressed: Al Gore, former US vice-president

explanation.surface: Someone tosses off a casual goodbye to Al Gore as a passing remark.
explanation.walkthrough: The farewell is addressed to Gore by his first name, so 'Later, Al' runs together into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Lateral describes movement or position to the side, as in a lateral pass, matching something set aside.

clue.text: One cross-channel article and another occupying leasing firm

parts.note: the French indefinite article, meaning one

indicators.note: a tenant occupying a home lives inside it, so this piece goes within the outer piece

parts.note: leasing out a property is renting it
another French article, the masculine definite one

explanation.surface: A French business and another company take space at a leasing firm's offices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leasing firm' looks like a company name; 'firm' is the definition and 'leasing' alone is wordplay. Cross-channel means French, from across the English Channel.
explanation.definitionFit: Firm in the sense of resolute and unyielding is matched by an adjective for refusing to soften or give way.

clue.text: Moulded plasticine, not initially stiff

indicators.note: not at the start means the opening letter is dropped
moulding reshapes material into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the modelling clay without its first letter

explanation.surface: Plasticine that has been worked into shape is no longer stiff.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests soft clay, yet the answer means the opposite of pliable.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that will not stretch or give is rigid and unyielding, so stiff describes it well.

clue.text: Ignoring the face, more beautiful frame

indicators.note: the face is the front, so ignoring it drops the first letter

parts.note: fair means beautiful, so more beautiful is the comparative

explanation.surface: A portrait painter skips the face but makes the frame more beautiful.
explanation.walkthrough: An airer is a folding rack for drying laundry, a common household item in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A clothes airer is a collapsible wooden or metal frame on which washing is hung to dry.

clue.text: House of Scandinavian clearing external angle

indicators.note: clearing away what sits on the outside leaves only the middle letters

parts.note: from Finland, loosely counted as Scandinavian
to angle is to fish

explanation.surface: A Nordic household clears a forest glade with an outer angle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clearing' looks like a forest glade but means removing, and 'external' says the removed letters sit at both ends, front and back, leaving the core. Finland is loosely grouped with Scandinavia.
explanation.definitionFit: A public house or tavern offering drink and lodging is an inn, and house is used for such places.

clue.text: Big guy turning tail, bitten by pig

indicators.note: turning round makes everything face the other way, so the order runs backwards
something bitten is held between the jaws, so it ends up enclosed

parts.note: a hog is a pig
taken as written

explanation.surface: A large man flees with a pig snapping at his backside.
explanation.walkthrough: The bite lands just after the pig's first letter, and 'turning' applies to the whole assembly, not just the tail.
explanation.definitionFit: Goliath is the Philistine giant slain by David, so his name stands for any very large man.

clue.text: Pot-holder about to exhaust last of incense

parts.note: re means concerning or about
to exhaust someone is to tire them

indicators.note: the last of something is its final element, so only the closing letter is kept

parts.note: final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone holding a pot of burning incense is about to use up the last of it.
explanation.walkthrough: Pot-holder suggests a kitchen glove or a censer, but the pot is a pension pot.
explanation.definitionFit: A pensioner draws on a pension pot, the savings fund built up over a working life, so is its holder.

clue.text: Pitch master showing alto line in repetitive composition

indicators.note: to be in something is to sit inside it, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: a rondo is a musical form whose main theme keeps recurring
A is the abbreviation for alto
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A choirmaster shows the alto part within a repetitive piece of music.
explanation.walkthrough: Pitch and alto set up a musical scene, but the pitch is a football pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Cristiano Ronaldo is one of the finest footballers ever, a master of the game on the field of play.

clue.text: Final order for AA lobbyist?

parts.note: surface: the last drink ordered before leaving the pub
setter's reading: the Automobile Association campaigns on behalf of motorists and highways, though AA also suggests Alcoholics Anonymous

explanation.walkthrough: AA is both Alcoholics Anonymous and the Automobile Association, a British motoring organisation; one lobbies against drink, the other for roads.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the idiom for a last drink before heading home, and literally a vote in favour of roads.

clue.text: Join up components of eleven Rolexes

indicators.note: components are parts of a larger whole, so the letters come from inside the words

parts.note: runs across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: Someone assembles the parts of eleven luxury watches.
explanation.walkthrough: Join up reads like assembling watch parts, but it is the definition, meaning to sign up.
explanation.definitionFit: To join up for a course or the army is to register formally as a member, which is what enrol means.

clue.text: High-flying business quickly capturing asteroid

indicators.note: capturing something means holding it inside, so one piece is enclosed

parts.note: apace means at speed
Eros is a well-known near-Earth asteroid

explanation.surface: A thriving company rushes to grab an asteroid for mining.
explanation.walkthrough: High-flying sounds like a successful firm, but it is literal: the industry builds aircraft and spacecraft.
explanation.definitionFit: The industry building aircraft, rockets and satellites works in flight through atmosphere and orbit, literally high-flying.

clue.text: Cut solo on soundstage for familiar actor

indicators.note: a soundstage is where sound is recorded, so we judge the words by how they are heard

parts.note: cut is sliced and solo is alone; said together they run into a famous name

explanation.surface: A film director cuts a solo scene shot on a studio soundstage for a well-known actor.
explanation.walkthrough: Familiar here means a nickname: Sylvester Stallone is widely known as Sly.
explanation.definitionFit: Sylvester Stallone, star of Rocky and Rambo, is an actor, and Sly is the familiar short form of his first name.

clue.text: In pursuit of wife, this Duke would be capital

parts.note: surface: a nobleman courting a woman; setter's reading: placed after W, the abbreviation for wife
with W in front the name becomes the capital of New Zealand, also the title of the Iron Duke

explanation.surface: A duke chasing a wife would think it splendid.
explanation.walkthrough: Capital in the surface means excellent; it really means a capital city. W is the standard abbreviation for wife.
explanation.definitionFit: Duke Ellington was the American jazz bandleader and composer, so this Duke names him.

clue.text: Maybe she'll bleat or nag crazily with Tannoy

indicators.note: acting crazily means behaving wildly, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written; a Tannoy is a public-address loudspeaker system in Britain

explanation.surface: A shrill woman complains or nags wildly over the public-address system.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a nagging person on a loudspeaker; the bleating is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: A female goat is a nanny, and goats bleat, so a nanny goat is one female creature that does it.

clue.text: Oik rounds on upper-class twit

indicators.note: one thing on another is placed next to it, here coming after it

parts.note: a yah is a braying upper-class person, from their way of saying yes
two round letters

explanation.surface: A lout turns on a posh fool and attacks him.
explanation.walkthrough: Oik is British slang for a coarse, ill-bred person, the opposite of the posh twit in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A yahoo is a boorish, uncouth person, from Swift's brutish creatures, which matches the British slang oik.

clue.text: Asian devouring starter of lentils and curry selection

indicators.note: whatever is devoured ends up inside the eater, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: a person from Thailand

indicators.note: a starter comes first, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the word's opening letter

explanation.surface: An Asian diner tucks into lentils first and then a selection of curries.
explanation.walkthrough: The food words make it look like a meal; only lentils gives a letter and Asian gives the outer word.
explanation.definitionFit: A thali is an Indian platter of several small dishes, typically curries, dal and rice, served together.

clue.text: A non-believer's caught out cleanly

definitions.note: cleanly here is the adjective meaning habitually clean

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: something out is no longer present, so the letter is removed

parts.note: a sceptic doubts or disbelieves
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: An atheist batsman is caught out neatly.
explanation.walkthrough: Cleanly looks like an adverb for the catch, but it is the old adjective meaning clean in habits.
explanation.definitionFit: Aseptic means free from germs and contamination, sterile, which fits the adjectival sense of clean.

clue.text: Speaker's fooled after Tories press together

indicators.note: after means following, so this piece comes second in the line

parts.note: Tories are Conservatives, abbreviated Cons

indicators.note: a speaker's version is the word as spoken, so we go by sound rather than spelling

parts.note: fooled is tricked

explanation.surface: The Commons Speaker was duped after Conservative MPs leaned on him.
explanation.walkthrough: Speaker suggests the Speaker of the House of Commons, but it signals sound.
explanation.definitionFit: To constrict is to squeeze or compress something, drawing its sides tighter, which is pressing it together.

clue.text: Flowers one penny each, with powder inside

indicators.note: inside means within, so one piece is placed in another

parts.note: Roman numeral one
P is the abbreviation for penny
Omo is a brand of washing powder sold in Britain
ea is the abbreviation for each

explanation.surface: A flower seller charges a penny per bloom, with powder sprinkled among them.
explanation.walkthrough: Flowers here is a plural used for a genus: morning glories.
explanation.definitionFit: Ipomoea is the plant genus of morning glories and sweet potato, known for trumpet-shaped blooms.

clue.text: Not quite coming out, unknown character's crisis

indicators.note: not quite complete means falling just short, so the final letter goes

parts.note: emergence, a coming out, shorn of its final letter
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A mysterious person is in turmoil about not quite coming out of the closet.
explanation.walkthrough: Coming out suggests revealing one's sexuality; here it is the noun for emerging.
explanation.definitionFit: An emergency is a sudden dangerous situation demanding urgent action, so it is a crisis.

clue.text: Minimum bill permitted in Northern Ireland

indicators.note: something permitted in has been let inside, so it sits within the other piece

parts.note: NIR is the official code for Northern Ireland
a bill is a poster or advertisement, an ad

explanation.surface: The lowest bill allowed under Northern Ireland's rules.
explanation.walkthrough: The usual crossword abbreviation for Northern Ireland is NI; this clue needs the three-letter code NIR.
explanation.definitionFit: The nadir is the lowest point of anything, the bottom, so it serves for a minimum.

clue.text: Left for good, nitwit is unattached

indicators.note: one thing for another means it stands in its place, so a letter is swapped

parts.note: L for left
G for good
a goose is a silly person

explanation.surface: Someone left for good, and now the fool is single.
explanation.walkthrough: Left for good reads as gone forever, but it says L replaces G.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose means not fastened or tied down, free of any fixing, which is being unattached.

clue.text: Flapper disturbing stray papers

indicators.note: to disturb things is to knock them out of their arrangement, so the letters move

parts.note: taken as written
identity papers, ID

explanation.surface: A 1920s flapper girl unsettles some scattered papers.
explanation.walkthrough: Flapper suggests a 1920s young woman; it is anything that flaps its wings.
explanation.definitionFit: A satyrid is a brown butterfly of the family that includes the ringlets and meadow browns, a creature that flaps.

clue.text: Scrap of fish chucked up

indicators.note: in a down entry, thrown upwards means read from the bottom, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: the gar is a long-snouted fish

explanation.surface: A morsel of fish someone has vomited up.
explanation.walkthrough: Up only reverses in a down clue, where the answer reads from top to bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: A rag is a small torn piece of cloth, so it can stand for a scrap or shred.

clue.text: A lot of aged Spanish gold provided aperitif

indicators.note: a lot of something is most but not all of it, so the final letter goes

parts.note: old, minus its last letter
oro is Spanish for gold
so, as in 'so long as', means provided

explanation.surface: Plenty of old Spanish gold was supplied along with a pre-dinner drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The aged Spanish gold sounds like doubloons, but the answer is a sherry.
explanation.definitionFit: Oloroso is a dark, rich style of Spanish sherry, the fortified wine often served before a meal.

clue.text: Doctor created tragic picture for smokers

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters are altered into a new order

parts.note: thirteen letters of fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A doctor paints a grim image warning smokers off.
explanation.walkthrough: Doctor looks like a physician behind a health warning; it is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Collectable illustrated cards were once packed in tobacco packets, giving smokers a small picture with each purchase.
